        "title": "Charts, tetrads, observer congruences and adapted charts in affine Minkowski space",
        "statement": "Work in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) with its inertial atlas (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas) and the canonical identification T_pA = V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v). The following objects are defined and are, in general, different objects. (a) Chart and inertial chart. A chart of the model is a diffeomorphism u: U -> u(U) from a nonempty open subset U of A onto an open subset of R^4 (def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds, def-smooth-manifold), written with components (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3). An inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) is the global chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p-o) of an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3). A general chart need not be inertial: if x is an inertial chart and N: x(U) -> R^4 is a diffeomorphism onto its image which is not the restriction of an affine map, then u := N o x is a chart that is not inertial, because if u were the inertial chart of a frame then x o u^{-1} = N^{-1} would be affine by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz and hence N = (N^{-1})^{-1} would be affine as the inverse of an affine bijection, a contradiction; the map N(y) = (y^0, y^1 + (y^0)^2, y^2, y^3) on R^4 is an explicit example. (b) Tetrad at an event and tetrad field. A tetrad at p in A is an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V with eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab} and e_0 future (e_0 in C^+); this is an inertial frame's basis without an origin and without the orientation condition. A tetrad field on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of smooth vector fields on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, type (1,0)) whose values at every p form a tetrad at p; it is observer-adapted when E_0 = U/c for a prescribed future timelike worldline or congruence. (c) Observer congruence. An observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A is a smooth vector field n: Omega -> V with eta(n,n) = -1 and n(p) in C^+ for all p; its observers are its maximal integral curves (def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field, thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point), each of which is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); n is nowhere zero because it is unit. Completeness of the integral curves, a global product structure of Omega and global synchronization are not asserted. (d) Adapted chart. For a congruence n on Omega, an n-adapted chart is a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 with U a nonempty open subset of Omega whose spatial coordinates u^1,u^2,u^3 are constant along every integral curve of n contained in U; no global adapted chart is asserted, and u^0 is not required to be affine. (e) Distinctions. A chart need not be inertial (a); a chart need not be n-adapted for any congruence; a tetrad field is not in general the coordinate frame of a chart: if (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) is the coordinate frame of a chart (v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3), i.e. E_a = partial/partial v^a, then [E_a,E_b] = 0 for all a,b (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields, prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket), so a tetrad field whose members do not commute pairwise is not a coordinate frame; no converse is claimed here. A congruence need not be a coordinate flow, and its pointwise rest spaces need not assemble into hypersurfaces; that integrability question is decided below on this page. In an inertial chart the coordinate frame is simultaneously an inertial frame's basis, a constant tetrad field and the congruence of stationary observers, but the four notions are distinct in general.",
        "strategy": "Definition item; well-definedness and consistency obligations. (i) The non-inertial chart example is checked through lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz: transitions between inertial charts are affine bijections, and the inverse of an affine bijection of R^4 is affine, so the polynomial coordinate change N cannot arise from an inertial frame; N is a diffeomorphism of R^4 because (z^0, z^1-(z^0)^2, z^2, z^3) is a smooth two-sided inverse. (ii) Tetrads exist at every point by lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis and lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist; a tetrad field is componentwise smooth in an inertial chart (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space). (iii) Maximal integral curves of a smooth field exist and are unique (thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point); a unit field is nowhere zero, so its curves are regular, and their future timelikeness is read pointwise from the causal classification and the time orientation. (iv) The commutation necessary condition for a coordinate frame is the coordinate formula for the Lie bracket. (v) No global assertions are made; the local adapted-chart and integrability questions are settled below on this page. All objects are finite-dimensional; no choice principle is used.",

        "title": "The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves",
        "statement": "Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so (Lambda^{-1})^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting the covariant derivative of each vector argument and also subtracting the covariant derivative of each covector argument; Precisely, for $T:(V^*)^r\\times V^s\\to\\mathbb R$, $(\\nabla_XT)(\\alpha_1,\\ldots,\\alpha_r;Y_1,\\ldots,Y_s)=X[T(\\alpha_1,\\ldots,\\alpha_r;Y_1,\\ldots,Y_s)]-\\sum_iT(\\alpha_1,\\ldots,\\nabla_X\\alpha_i,\\ldots,\\alpha_r;Y_1,\\ldots,Y_s)-\\sum_jT(\\alpha_1,\\ldots,\\alpha_r;Y_1,\\ldots,\\nabla_XY_j,\\ldots,Y_s)$. In inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of that component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation. (e) First-order C1 version. For C1 vector fields X,Y and C1 covector/tensor fields on Omega, the same directional/evaluation definitions are well-defined and have continuous coefficients: in an inertial chart $(\\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\\partial_bY^a$ and each tensor component is differentiated in the same way. The component recovery and subtraction of all argument derivatives remain valid. C1 scalar multiplication satisfies the same first-order Leibniz rules, metric compatibility remains $\\nabla\\eta=0$, and the first-order torsion identity uses the continuous coordinate bracket $[X,Y]^a=X^b\\partial_bY^a-Y^b\\partial_bX^a$. No C1 closure of this bracket or second covariant derivative of arbitrary C1 data is asserted. For C2 vector fields the second derivatives needed for the zero-curvature identity in(c) exist, and that identity follows by equality of the continuous mixed second partials. All original smooth-field properties and the C1 along-curve derivative in(d) are retained.",
        "strategy": "Definition with well-definedness obligations. (i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the corrected identity X'^b partial'_b Y'^a=Lambda^a_c X^b partial_b Y^c, equivalently inverse-Lambda recovery of the unprimed components, using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in(b) subtracts the derivative of every argument, whether vector or covector. In an inertial chart use the constant coordinate basis and constant dual basis; their covariant derivatives vanish, so evaluating the rule on those bases leaves only X acting on each tensor component. For variable arguments the ordinary product rule cancels all their derivatives with the displayed subtractions. This proves the stated coordinate formula and the evaluation derivation rule; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. (iv) In (d), the canonical isomorphism T_pA = V is independent of p, so the covariant derivative along a curve coincides with the ordinary derivative and parallel transport is trivial; this is exactly what makes Fermi-Walker transport below an ordinary linear ODE. No choice principle is used. For(e), a C1 map Y has continuous differential, and differentiating $Y(p+tX(p))$ at zero gives $dY_p[X(p)]$; the continuous product of dY and X yields the claimed C0 field. The coordinate tensor rule is identical on constant bases, with the ordinary C1 product rule for variable arguments. Only first derivatives occur in the C1 Leibniz/metric/torsion assertions. When X,Y,Z are C2, the fields $\\nabla_YZ$ and $\\nabla_XZ$ are C1, so the two iterated derivatives and the bracket term in the curvature identity are defined; expansion cancels the first-order bracket terms and the remaining mixed second partials commute.         "statement": "Let n be an observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction), let nabla be the flat covariant derivative (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), and write n_b := eta_{bc} n^c for the associated covector field. (a) Rest metric and projection. Define h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) for vectors at the same point, so h = eta + n-flat (x) n-flat; then h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) where h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n is the orthogonal projection of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). At every point h is symmetric with radical spanned by n(p), and its restriction to n(p)^perp is positive definite. (b) Acceleration. The acceleration of the congruence is a := nabla_n n; then eta(n,a) = 0 pointwise, because 2 eta(n, nabla_n n) = n(eta(n,n)) = 0, so a(p) is spacelike or zero by the causal classification. In the model's physical interpretation the four-acceleration of the congruence observers is c^2 a and its magnitude is c^2 sqrt(eta(a,a)); the numerical units belong to the model's SI conventions and are not part of the affine geometry. (c) Kinematic decomposition. Set theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and omega_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c} n_{d]}, where nabla_{(c} n_{d)} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d + nabla_d n_c) and nabla_{[c} n_{d]} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d - nabla_d n_c). Then nabla_a n_b = -n_a a_b + theta_{ab} + omega_{ab}, with theta symmetric, omega antisymmetric, both horizontal (theta_{ab} n^b = omega_{ab} n^b = n^a theta_{ab} = n^a omega_{ab} = 0), and this decomposition is unique with these properties. theta is the expansion (and shear) tensor, theta := h^{ab} theta_{ab} is the expansion scalar, its trace-free part is the shear, and omega is the vorticity 2-tensor. (d) Born rigidity. The congruence is Born rigid (describes a rigid motion) if L_n h = 0. Since (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, Born rigidity is equivalent to theta = 0, equivalently to the projected symmetrized derivative of n-flat vanishing. (e) Scope. These are kinematic definitions for a prescribed smooth field n on the affine model; no dynamical equation, matter model, global synchronization or completeness is assumed, and a, theta, omega and h are local objects on Omega.",
